title: Ind AS 10 "Events after the Reporting Period"
outcomes: Identify the period covered by Ind AS 10.
Account for dividends and going concern issues after year end.

meta.exam_tip: Ask "did the condition exist at year end?" — yes means adjust, no means disclose.

concepts.title: Meaning and period of events after the reporting period
body: Ind AS 10 deals with good and bad events falling after the year-end date but before the Board authorises the statements for issue.

The date of approval is the date the Board (or equivalent) authorises issue — even if shareholders approve later. Entities disclose the approval date and who gave it; if owners can amend statements after issue, that fact is disclosed.
Events after the approval date are outside the standard; the statements are not updated for them.
concepts.analogy: Ind AS 10 covers the window between the balance sheet date and Board approval.
concepts.work: For a 31 March year end with Board approval on 20 May, events until 20 May count.

concepts.title: Adjusting events
body: Adjusting events throw light on circumstances already present on the year-end date, so the recognised amounts are changed.

Examples: settlement of a court case confirming an obligation at year end; information that an asset was impaired at year end (a customer's bankruptcy, sale of inventory below cost); determination after year end of the cost of assets bought or proceeds of assets sold before year end; profit-sharing or bonus payments for which there was a present obligation; and discovery of fraud or errors showing the statements are incorrect.
Disclosures relating to conditions at year end are updated for new information.
concepts.analogy: Adjusting events shed new light on what was already true at year end.
concepts.work: A debtor's insolvency in April usually reflects difficulties that existed in March.

concepts.title: Non-adjusting events and disclosure
body: Non-adjusting events indicate conditions that arose after the reporting period; amounts are not adjusted.

Examples: a decline in the fair value of investments after year end; major business combinations or disposals; announcing a plan to discontinue an operation; major asset purchases; destruction of a plant by fire; major restructuring announced; large share transactions; abnormal changes in prices or exchange rates; changes in tax rates enacted after year end; entering significant commitments; and litigation arising solely from post-year-end events.
For each material non-adjusting event, the nature and an estimate of the financial effect (or a statement that it cannot be estimated) is disclosed.
concepts.analogy: Non-adjusting events are new stories — they are told in the notes, not in the numbers.
concepts.work: A tax rate increase enacted in April does not change deferred tax measured at 31 March.

concepts.title: Dividends and going concern
body: Dividends declared (proposed) after the reporting period are not recognised as a liability at year end because no obligation existed then; they are disclosed in the notes.

If, after the reporting period, management decides to liquidate or cease trading, or has no realistic alternative, the statements are not prepared on a going concern basis. A deterioration in results and financial position after year end may signal a going concern problem that needs reassessment.
Where the going concern basis is not appropriate, the effect is pervasive — it changes the basis of accounting, not just individual amounts.
concepts.analogy: A proposed dividend is a plan, not a debt; a going concern collapse changes everything.
concepts.work: If the Board decides in May to close the company, the March statements cannot use the going concern basis.

illustrations.title: Adjust or disclose?
illustrations.q: Year end 31 March 2027; statements approved for issue 18 May 2027. Classify: (a) on 20 April a customer owing ₹2 crore at 31 March is declared bankrupt; its financial trouble began in January; (b) on 25 April a fire destroys a warehouse; (c) on 2 May a court confirms that the company must pay ₹80 lakh for a case filed in 2026 (provision at year end: ₹50 lakh); (d) inventory held at 31 March is sold in April below cost; (e) on 10 May the Board proposes a final dividend; (f) on 5 June a major acquisition is agreed.

head: Event
Type
Treatment
rows: Evidence of impairment existing at 31 March — recognise loss allowance
Condition arose after year end — disclose nature and estimated effect if material
Confirms a present obligation at year end — increase provision to ₹80 lakh
Evidence of net realisable value at year end — write down inventory
No liability at 31 March — disclose in notes
Occurs after approval date — not considered
solution.title: Ind AS 10

illustrations.title: Inventory sold below cost after year end
illustrations.q: 4,000 units held at 31 March cost ₹120 each. In April they are sold at ₹100 each with selling costs of ₹5 per unit. Compute the write-down to recognise at 31 March.

jobs.title: Subsequent events review
jobs.situation: The audit report is due next week; the year ended six weeks ago.
steps: Read Board minutes after year end.
Review post-year-end sales, receipts and legal letters.
Classify each event as adjusting or non-adjusting.
Confirm the approval date and update disclosures.
jobs.takeaway: The review runs until the approval date, not just the year end.

mcqs.q: Events after the reporting period cover the period up to:
options: The date the statements are approved for issue
mcqs.explain: The cut-off is the Board's approval for issue. In practice: disclose that date.
mcqs.topic: Meaning and period of events after the reporting period

options: Settlement of a court case confirming a year-end obligation
A fall in share prices after year end
A new acquisition after year end
mcqs.explain: It gives evidence of a condition at year end. In practice: adjust the provision.

mcqs.q: A dividend proposed by the Board after year end is:
options: Disclosed, not recognised as a liability
mcqs.explain: There was no obligation at the reporting date. In practice: show in notes with per share amount.

mcqs.q: A change in tax rate enacted after the reporting date is:
mcqs.explain: Measurement uses rates enacted or substantively enacted at year end. In practice: disclose the effect.

mcqs.q: Discovery after year end of a fraud that occurred during the year is:
mcqs.explain: It shows the statements are incorrect as at year end. In practice: correct the amounts.

mcqs.q: If management decides to liquidate the entity after year end:
options: The going concern basis is not used
mcqs.explain: The going concern basis becomes inappropriate. In practice: a different basis is applied and disclosed.

mcqs.q: For a material non-adjusting event, the entity discloses:
options: Its nature and an estimate of financial effect
mcqs.explain: Or states that an estimate cannot be made. In practice: keep it specific.

mcqs.q: An event occurring after the statements are approved for issue is:
mcqs.explain: The standard's window closes at approval. In practice: may be reported next year.

model.title: Ind AS 10

remarks: Give the condition test each time.

questions.q: 4,000 units held at 31 March cost ₹120 each. In April they are sold at ₹100 each with selling costs of ₹5 per unit. Compute the write-down to recognise at 31 March.

summary: Window: reporting date to approval for issue.
Non-adjusting: new conditions — disclose nature and effect.
Liquidation decision → no going concern basis.
traps: Post-year-end tax rate changes are non-adjusting.

viva.q: Define events after the reporting period.
viva.model: Good and bad events occurring after the year-end date and before the Board authorises the statements for issue.

viva.q: What distinguishes adjusting from non-adjusting events?
viva.model: Adjusting events give evidence of conditions existing at the reporting date; non-adjusting events show conditions that arose after it.
Destruction of a plant by fire after year end and a major business combination after year end.

viva.q: Why is a proposed dividend not a liability?
viva.model: Because the duty to pay comes into being only once it is declared after year end, so at the reporting date there was nothing owed.

viva.q: What must be disclosed about approval?
viva.model: The date of authorisation for issue, the body that authorised it (usually the Board), and whether owners have power to amend the statements afterwards.

cases.title: Narmada Chemicals Ltd.
cases.case: Narmada Chemicals Ltd. (year end 31 March 2027; approval 22 May 2027): in April it learns that a key supplier's plant was shut by regulators in February, raising its own input costs from June; in April its investment in listed shares falls 30%; on 10 May its insurance claim for a March flood is settled at ₹40 lakh more than the receivable recorded; on 15 May it announces a plan to close one division.

mcqs.q: The 30% fall in listed shares in April is:
mcqs.explain: Market value changes after year end reflect later conditions. In practice: disclose if material.

mcqs.q: The higher insurance settlement for the March flood is:
options: Adjusting — it gives evidence of the year-end receivable
mcqs.explain: The claim relates to an event at year end; settlement determines the amount. In practice: update the receivable.

mcqs.q: Announcing the division closure on 15 May is:
mcqs.explain: A plan announced after year end does not change year-end amounts. In practice: Ind AS 105/37 apply next year.

mcqs.q: If instead the Board decided on 15 May to wind up the whole company:
options: The statements would not be prepared on a going concern basis
mcqs.explain: A decision to liquidate before approval removes the going concern basis. In practice: pervasive change.
